sourceRegulation: NYDFS 23 NYCRR Part 500 (Cybersecurity Requirements for Financial Services Companies), as amended by the Second Amendment (eff. 2023-11-01; fully in force 2025-11-01)
note: Field names inferred from the Transformation Bridge UI. Confirm against the real import schema before load. 'nydfsSections', 'classAOnly', and 'sdlcGates' are extension fields for traceability. 'classAOnly: true' marks obligations that apply only if Meridian is a Class A company (§500.1(d)) — confirm that determination first (see INTEGRATION-NOTES).

standards.whatItMeans: Maintain a risk-based cybersecurity program performing the six core functions (identify, protect, detect, respond, recover, and fulfil regulatory reporting). Class A companies must design and conduct independent audits of the program.

Maintain written cybersecurity policies approved at least annually by a senior officer or the senior governing body, covering data governance/classification/retention, asset inventory, access, BCDR, network security/monitoring, app security, vendor management, risk assessment, incident response, and vulnerability management.

Designate a CISO who reports in writing at least annually to the senior governing body and timely on material issues; the senior governing body exercises documented oversight of cyber risk (understanding, direction, review of reports, resourcing).

Written policies ensuring penetration testing from inside and outside system boundaries by a qualified party at least annually, automated scans plus manual review at a risk-based cadence and after material changes, a monitoring process for new vulnerabilities, and timely risk-prioritized remediation. Class A: external expert involvement.
Maintain systems that reconstruct material financial transactions (retain at least 5 years) and audit trails that detect and respond to material cybersecurity events (retain at least 3 years).

Enforce least privilege; limit the number, scope, and use of privileged accounts; review all access at least annually and remove what is unnecessary; disable remote-control protocols; promptly terminate access on departure; maintain a password policy meeting industry standards. Class A: privileged-access management solution and automated blocking of commonly used passwords.

Maintain written secure-development procedures, guidelines, and standards for in-house applications, and procedures to evaluate, assess, and test the security of externally developed applications; reviewed at least annually by the CISO or a qualified designee.
Conduct a documented, periodic risk assessment that informs the program; review and update it at least annually and whenever a business or technology change materially changes cyber risk.

Use qualified cybersecurity personnel (in-house, affiliate, or provider) sufficient to manage risk; provide updates and training; verify key personnel maintain current threat and countermeasure knowledge.

Maintain written TPSP policies covering identification/risk assessment, minimum required practices, due diligence, and periodic reassessment; contractual guidelines on the provider's MFA, encryption, and breach-notice obligations.

Require MFA for any individual accessing any information system (limited-exemption entities at minimum for remote access, remote third-party apps exposing NPI, and privileged accounts). CISO may approve equivalent or stronger compensating controls, reviewed at least annually.

Maintain written policies that produce and keep a complete, accurate, documented asset inventory of information systems, tracking owner, location, classification/sensitivity, support-expiration date, and recovery-time objectives, plus the update/validation frequency.

Maintain policies for the secure periodic disposal of NPI (personal-identifier and health categories) that is no longer needed for business operations, unless retention is legally required or targeted disposal is not reasonably feasible.

Implement risk-based controls to monitor authorized-user activity and detect unauthorized access/use/tampering, and to protect against malicious code including web-traffic and email filtering. Class A: endpoint detection & response plus a centralized logging / security-event-alerting (SIEM) solution.
Provide periodic, at least annual, cybersecurity awareness training that includes social engineering for all personnel, updated to reflect risks identified in the risk assessment.

Maintain a written encryption policy meeting industry standards to protect NPI in transit over external networks and at rest; where at-rest encryption is infeasible, use CISO-approved compensating controls reviewed at least annually.

Maintain a written incident response plan addressing goals, internal processes, roles and decision authority, communications, remediation, documentation, recovery from backups, and a root-cause analysis; covering disruptive events such as ransomware; tested at least annually.

Maintain written BCDR plans that ensure availability of information systems and material services; identify essential assets and personnel; maintain protected, offsite backups; distribute and train on the plans; test the plans and backup-restore at least annually.

Notify the superintendent electronically no later than 72 hours after determining a cybersecurity incident has occurred at the entity, an affiliate, or a third-party service provider, with a continuing duty to update.

On an extortion payment, notify the superintendent within 24 hours and within 30 days provide a written description of why payment was necessary, alternatives considered, and OFAC compliance diligence.

By April 15, submit either a Certification of Material Compliance (backed by sufficient data and documentation) or a written Acknowledgment of noncompliance identifying gaps and a remediation timeline; signed by the highest-ranking executive and the CISO; supporting records retained 5 years.

Identify and classify Nonpublic Information (material business information; personal identifiers combined with SSN/licence/financial/security codes/biometrics; and health information) so that access, encryption, retention, monitoring, and audit-trail controls can be correctly scoped.
